title: How to Hit Your Protein Goals on a NZ Budget – Cheapest Protein per Gram
meta_desc: Discover the cheapest NZ protein sources per gram at Pak'nSave, Woolworths and Countdown. Practical tips to meet your protein targets without breaking the bank.
intro: Getting enough protein doesn’t have to cost a fortune. This guide breaks down the most affordable NZ supermarket options, shows you the cost per gram of protein and gives you simple meal ideas you can start this week.

sections.heading: Why Protein Matters for Gym‑Goers
sections.body: Protein is the building block for muscle repair, growth and recovery after resistance training. New Zealand research shows that athletes who meet their protein needs recover faster and see greater strength gains (NZ Sports Institute, 2024). The recommended intake for active adults is 1.6–2.2 g per kilogram of body weight per day, but many gym‑goers fall short because they rely on expensive cuts of meat or specialised supplements.

sections.heading: Calculate Your Daily Target
sections.body: First, work out how much protein you need. Multiply your body weight (kg) by 1.8 g for a middle‑ground target. For example, a 75 kg lifter would aim for about 135 g of protein each day. Split this across 3–5 meals to keep amino acid levels steady and support muscle protein synthesis.
list: Spread across meals (e.g., 30 g per meal)
Adjust up if you’re in a calorie deficit or training twice daily

sections.heading: Build a Budget‑Friendly Protein Meal Plan
sections.body: Use the low‑cost items above to hit your target without buying pricey supplements. Here are three easy meals you can prep in under 30 minutes:
list: Breakfast: 3 scrambled eggs + 100 g sautéed lentils – ~30 g protein
Lunch: Tuna salad (1 can tuna, 150 g mixed veg, 2 tbsp low‑fat mayo) – ~35 g protein
Dinner: Roast chicken thighs (200 g) with Greek yoghurt dip and a side of boiled lentils – ~40 g protein

sections.heading: Money‑Saving Hacks for Protein
sections.body: Even the cheapest sources can stretch further with a few smart habits. These tips keep costs low and nutrition high:
list: Buy in bulk when there’s a sale – freeze extra chicken thighs in portion bags
Choose store‑brand canned tuna; it’s usually 10‑15 % cheaper than name brands
Swap fresh yoghurt for bulk Greek yoghurt tubs and portion into smaller containers
Rinse lentils before cooking to reduce anti‑nutrients and improve digestibility
If you’re a member of Exercise NZ’s subsidised gym scheme, you may qualify for a 40‑70 % discount on gym fees, freeing up more of your budget for food
